claims_consolidated.text: Halbwachs' theory establishes that collective memory functions only within social group frameworks, with different groups maintaining distinct historical narratives

confidence_history.reason: Multiple academic sources confirm Halbwachs' foundational framework
Confirmed by 100+ years of scholarly consensus; theory foundational and unshaken
Consolidation and packaging: foundational theory, 100+ year stability confirmed

claims_consolidated.notes: Foundational to modern memory studies. Theory developed early 20th century before contemporary psychology; updated frameworks may refine but not invalidate.

claims_consolidated.text: Assmann distinguishes between communicative memory (80-100 year span, informal) and cultural memory (institutionalized, ritual-based transmission)

confidence_history.reason: Boundaries between communicative/cultural memory are contested in some scholarly circles; 80-100 year span is average, not universal; some cultures maintain 150+ year communicative memory chains
Consolidation: core distinction sound but boundary fuzzier than sometimes presented. Requires caveat in narration: '80-100 year span is statistical norm but culture-dependent'.

claims_consolidated.notes: Central distinction in cultural memory studies. Red-team flag: EVIDENCE_INFLATION on 80-100 year boundary being presented as universal rule; actually culture-dependent.
claims_consolidated.d2_qualification: CONDITIONAL - requires caveat in production: 'Generally 80-100 years, but varies by cultural context'

claims_consolidated.text: Intergenerational transmission breakdown (parents raising children in dominant language) is the critical tipping point for language extinction

confidence_history.reason: Language revivals (Hebrew, Basque) show transmission interruption is not irreversible; claim identifies tipping point correctly but may understate reversibility with sustained intervention
Consolidation: directionally correct; language-loss mechanisms verified. Caveat: tipping point can be reversed with intentional effort (language revivals precedent).

claims_consolidated.notes: Key mechanism of language loss identified. Directional claim sound; may understate reversibility.
claims_consolidated.d2_qualification: READY - mechanism established; reversibility caveat noted but does not invalidate primary claim about tipping point existence

causal_links.cause_event: Collective memory formation within social group frameworks (C-A-001)

causal_reasoning.temporal_relationship: Group-level memory prerequisite to individual transmission
causal_reasoning.mechanism: Halbwachs framework shows social group frameworks necessary for collective memory; communicative memory (C-A-002) depends on group transmission chains; transmission failure breaks these chains

causal_links.note: Logical chain: collective memory (group) → communicative memory (80-100 yr span, informal) → intergenerational transmission → language survival. Breaking any link stops the chain.
